title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 notes (Chapter IX, 'Ateliers') on a combinatorial approach to topology. The basic object is a set M of 'figures' or 'structures', for example the cells of a combinatorial space or the intervals of an ordered set. M carries:
- an incidence relation (written Δ or ⊴);
- a 'face/inclusion' order ≤°;
- a realization or support |·|;
- for each X, a fragment X̃ (roughly the closure or star of X).

Two extra data are compared:
1. A compactology M_c ⊂ M: the figures declared 'compact'.
2. An atelier F attached to M: an admissible class of fragments (subsets of M closed under certain operations, like subcomplexes).

The link between them is the relation 'X meets Y' (written \overline{||}). A subset L is locally finite for M_c if every compact X meets only finitely many members of L.

Previous page. Given M_c, the locally finite fragments F_lf(M) form the largest atelier compatible with M_c. Axiom Mégacrit 4 c) says that each X̃ is locally finite. Conversely, given F, he defines M_c = {X | for all F ∈ F, {Y ∈ F | X meets Y} is finite}, the largest compactology compatible with F. This is a Galois connection (an antitone pair) induced by the relation 'meets only finitely many'.

This page.
- He checks that this M_c satisfies axioms Mégacrit 1 a), b), c). For a) and c) it suffices to take F = X̃.
- If F consists of finite figures, every X qualifies, so M_c = M is the largest compactology.
- He then rejects defining M_c intrinsically from (M, ⊴, ≤°, |·|) alone, e.g. as {X | for all Y, {Y' ∈ Ỹ | Y' meets X} is finite}. That would give M_c = M whenever all the Ỹ are finite.
- Counterexample: an ordered set I with one end or no end (an interval that is not a segment). There one naturally wants only the points a and the closed intervals I_{a,b} to be compact, not rays or I itself.
- Conclusion: the compactology is a genuine extra datum, more interesting than the choice of any particular attached atelier.

Next page. The compactology yields compact figures and locally finite figures. In practice only three ateliers matter: finite figures, locally finite figures, and (at a pinch) all figures. The right framework is therefore a 'compactological' structure (M, ⊴, ≤°, |·|, M_c). The problem served is axiomatizing a finitary/combinatorial topology in which 'compact support' and 'locally finite' are both available, as for ordinary chains versus Borel–Moore (locally finite) chains.
errors: No mathematical error. The statement 'if F is formed of finite figures, M_c is the largest compactology' is correct but trivial: every X then meets each F in a finite set, so M_c = M.
For a) and c), taking F = X̃ presupposes X̃ ∈ F, i.e. M ⊂ F (the previous page notes this requirement). This is an implicit hypothesis.
The machine transcription has several misreadings, listed under transcription_corrections.

ideas.what: Galois-type duality between a class of 'compact' figures and a class of admissible fragments, via the relation 'X meets only finitely many members of F'. Locally finite fragments form the largest atelier for a given compactology; conversely there is a largest compactology for a given atelier.
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity; compact support vs locally finite (cf. bornologies, coarse structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: General Galois connections: Birkhoff/Ore. Bornologies: Hogbe-Nlend. Abstract compactologies: Waelbroeck, Buchwalter (functional analysis). Coarse structures: Roe.

ideas.what: Design decision: the compactology must be an independent datum, not definable from the incidence structure alone. Illustrated by the half-open or open discrete interval, where only points and closed intervals should be compact.
ideas.modern_name: Choice of compact-support structure in combinatorial/locally finite complexes (proper vs ordinary homotopy, Borel–Moore vs ordinary chains)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (locally finite CW/simplicial complexes, proper homotopy theory)

ideas.what: Combinatorial-topology framework of 'multistructures', 'ateliers', axioms 'Mégacrit' and 'compactological' data (M, ⊴, ≤°, |·|, M_c), proposed as the frame for a combinatorial approach to topology.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic combinatorial / tame topology (related in spirit to face posets, cellular structures, o-minimal tame topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart; tame topology was programmatically proposed in Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984).
ideas.where_published: Related programmatic remarks on tame topology in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific formalism is not known to be published.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'ateliers / compactologies' formalism for a combinatorial topology is an unpublished, apparently unexplored axiomatic framework. In it, compactness is an extra structure on a set of figures, dual to the class of locally finite fragments. The page records the decision to make the compactology primary rather than the atelier.
missed.quote: Il semble bien que ce soit la donnée supplémentaire de la compactologie, qui soit une structure souvent plus intéressante que celle d'un atelier attenant particulier.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a direct trace of how Grothendieck tried to realize the 'tame topology' programme of the Esquisse combinatorially. Comparison with coarse geometry and bornologies (locally finite / uniformly finite homology) or with o-minimal definable cell structures could be of historical and possibly technical interest. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: An unpublished design discussion within an obscure combinatorial-topology formalism. The mathematical content (a Galois correspondence between compact elements and locally finite families, plus a simple counterexample) is routine. Its interest is mainly as documentation of the unpublished 1986 framework.
transcription_corrections: 'les conditions $M_{\geq}$ cf. et 1 a) b) c)' should read 'les conditions Mégacrit 1 a) b) c)'.
'(pour a), et c), il prendre F = X̃)' is better read '(pour a) et c), il suffit de prendre F = X̃)'.
'le plus grand des convictologies' should read 'la plus grande des compactologies'.
The ingredients are likely '(M, Δ/⊴, ≤°, |·|)', matching the previous page; '\mathring{i}c' is a misreading of the order symbol ≤°.
'Y' \overline{\amalg} X' is the same 'meets' relation written \overline{||} on the previous page.
'toutes les multistructures de Ỹ de M' is uncertain; probably 'toutes les [figures] Ỹ de M sont finies'.
'les seules structures de la forme a' is probably 'les seules figures de la forme a (a∈I), I_{a,b}'.

'ce soit le domaine d'aujourd'hui de la convictologie, qui soit une structure sensible plus intéressante que celles décrites ci-dessus particulier' should read 'ce soit la donnée supplémentaire de la compactologie, qui soit une structure souvent plus intéressante que celle d'un atelier attenant particulier'.
